_note: The runway checks' figures from the Cessna 172S POH's own tables and notes, SAFO 19001, the AIM and NASR's codes, never from the code. The POH tables are data/aircraft/c172.json's, written once under `shared`. Shape and checks as engine/facade/tests/common/cases.rs says; asked by engine/facade/tests/rule_cases.rs.

takeoff.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-5: short field, flaps 10°, paved, level and dry
takeoff.wind_source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), notes to figures 5-5 and 5-11: decrease distances 10% for each 9 knots headwind; with tail winds up to 10 knots, increase distances by 10% for each 2 knots

landing.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-11: short field, flaps 30°, paved, level and dry
landing.wind_source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), notes to figures 5-5 and 5-11: decrease distances 10% for each 9 knots headwind; with tail winds up to 10 knots, increase distances by 10% for each 2 knots

cases.name: Sea level, 10 C, 2,550 lb, still air: the table's own 925 and 1,575 ft
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-5, short field takeoff distance, flaps 10, paved, level and dry (the table as data/aircraft/c172.json keeps it).

cases.name: 9 kt of headwind takes 10 per cent off
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-5, short field takeoff distance, flaps 10, paved, level and dry (the table as data/aircraft/c172.json keeps it), and its notes: "Decrease distances 10% for each 9 knots headwind. For operation with tail winds up to 10 knots, increase distances by 10% for each 2 knots."

cases.name: 2 kt of tailwind adds 10 per cent
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-5, short field takeoff distance, flaps 10, paved, level and dry (the table as data/aircraft/c172.json keeps it), and its notes: "Decrease distances 10% for each 9 knots headwind. For operation with tail winds up to 10 knots, increase distances by 10% for each 2 knots."

cases.name: Between the rows and columns: 500 ft and 15 C, read straight between
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-5, short field takeoff distance, flaps 10, paved, level and dry (the table as data/aircraft/c172.json keeps it); FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 11, performance charts: a figure between a table's entries is interpolated.

cases.name: Grass adds 15 per cent of the ground roll
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-5, short field takeoff distance, flaps 10, paved, level and dry (the table as data/aircraft/c172.json keeps it), and its note: "For operation on dry, grass runway, increase distances by 15% of the 'ground roll' figure."

cases.name: At 2,400 lb, the lighter table
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-5, short field takeoff distance, flaps 10, paved, level and dry (the table as data/aircraft/c172.json keeps it), its 2,400 lb table.

cases.name: No weight known: the heaviest table, the longest distance
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-5, short field takeoff distance, flaps 10, paved, level and dry (the table as data/aircraft/c172.json keeps it); 14 CFR 91.103(b): with the weight not known, the safer figure.

cases.name: Past the table's 8,000 ft: said to be beyond it
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-5, short field takeoff distance, flaps 10, paved, level and dry (the table as data/aircraft/c172.json keeps it): the table stops at 8,000 ft; nothing past it is the POH's, so it is said, and never less than its last row (FAA-H-8083-25C ch. 11: a chart is valid only within its stated conditions).

cases.name: A runway shorter than the distance over 50 ft is over
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-5, short field takeoff distance, flaps 10, paved, level and dry (the table as data/aircraft/c172.json keeps it): 1,575 ft over 50 ft against 1,500 ft of runway.

cases.name: A tailwind past the POH's 10 kt is said
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-5, short field takeoff distance, flaps 10, paved, level and dry (the table as data/aircraft/c172.json keeps it), and its notes: "Decrease distances 10% for each 9 knots headwind. For operation with tail winds up to 10 knots, increase distances by 10% for each 2 knots." Nothing is given past 10 knots.

cases.name: Landing at sea level, 10 C: 565 and 1,320 ft
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-11, short field landing distance, flaps 30.

cases.name: Landing on grass adds 45 per cent of the ground roll
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-11, short field landing distance, flaps 30, and its note: "For operation on dry, grass runway, increase distances by 45% of the 'ground roll' figure."

cases.name: 360 at 12 gusting 20 across 27: 20 kt across, over the demonstrated 15
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998) section 4: maximum demonstrated crosswind velocity 15 knots. The gust's crosswind, straight across.

cases.name: 15 kt straight across: at the demonstrated, not over it
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998) section 4: maximum demonstrated crosswind velocity 15 knots.

cases.name: A variable wind may all be across
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998) section 4: maximum demonstrated crosswind velocity 15 knots. AIM 7-1-28: VRB is a wind of no steady direction, so any of it, the gusts too, may blow straight across (the safer side).

cases.name: A runway a foot short of the distance over 50 ft is short
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998), figure 5-5, short field takeoff distance, flaps 10, paved, level and dry (the table as data/aircraft/c172.json keeps it); 29.92 inHg at sea level is a pressure altitude of 0 (FAA-H-8083-25C Figure 11-22).

cases.name: Within SAFO 19001's 15 per cent: close
cases.source: SAFO 19001 (2019), landing performance: a 15 per cent margin over the distance the manufacturer's data gives; 1.10 of the distance is inside 1.15.

cases.name: Past the 15 per cent: neither short nor close
cases.source: SAFO 19001 (2019), landing performance: a 15 per cent margin over the distance the manufacturer's data gives.

cases.name: A landing has the runway past its displaced threshold
cases.source: AIM 2-3-3: "The portion of runway behind a displaced threshold is available for takeoffs in either direction and landings from the opposite direction."

cases.name: A takeoff has all of it
cases.source: AIM 2-3-3, as the landing case.

cases.name: No elevation: the fit is not known, never read as fitting
cases.source: 14 CFR 91.103(b): runway lengths and takeoff and landing distance data; with no elevation there is no pressure altitude to read the table at.

cases.name: The departure's check: a variable 12 gusting 22 may be 22 across, over the 15
cases.source: Cessna 172S POH (1998) section 4: maximum demonstrated crosswind velocity 15 knots. AIM 7-1-28 VRB; FAA-H-8083-25C Figure 11-22, 29.92 inHg is the standard datum.

cases.name: TURF is soft
cases.source: NASR APT_RWY.csv SURFACE_TYPE_CODE: TURF, GRVL and DIRT unpaved; ASPH and CONC paved (the POH's grass correction is for an unpaved runway).
